title: Routine tag run overlapped the echopoint deploy gate: flow folders 409 FLOW_TREE_CONFLICT
summary: At 18:34Z the routine's second ad-hoc soak of the `echopoint` tag ran while Deploy Router run 42401825800 (echopoint#779) was running the same tag as its post-deploy gate. Both runs use the prod CI org and its `echopointOrgId`. The flow-tree lock (`pglock.TryAdvisoryXactLock` on `echopoint.flow_tree:<org>`) rejects a second writer at once instead of waiting, so the routine's `flow folders` flow got **409 FLOW_TREE_CONFLICT** on `cleanup-sibling`. The gate stayed green and promoted prod at 18:37Z, but only because its own `flow folders` won the lock. `run_suites.sh` now waits for any active Deploy Router run before each tag and flags any overlap.

impact.text: No customer impact and no held deploy. One routine soak run read 56/57 instead of 57/57. Had the gate's `flow folders` lost the lock instead, the gate would have gone red and held echopoint#779 off prod until a human reran it.

numbers.label: overlap of routine run and gate suite

trigger: An ad-hoc `echopoint` tag run (soak of a newly tagged flow) started at 18:35Z without checking for an active Deploy Router run; the gate's suite for echopoint#779 had started at 18:33:37Z.
detection: The routine read its own tag result (56/57) and matched the failing execution's start time against the gate's job times. Detection was good enough for this side; the new `GATE-OVERLAP` line in `run_suites.sh` now names the overlap directly.
resolution: The routine reran the tag once the gate finished (57/57) and added `gate_wait` and `gate_overlap` to `run_suites.sh`, so scheduled runs never start a tag while a Deploy Router run is queued or in progress.
contributing: SKILL.md says not to run tags during a gate, but nothing enforced it.
Soaks after tagging were run by hand with `flows run --tag`, outside `run_suites.sh`.
The tree lock fails fast; any two writers to the folder tree in one org conflict.
The dogfood suites and the post-deploy gate share one CI org and one `echopointOrgId`.

messaging.internal: The routine's tag soak overlapped the echopoint gate and its `flow folders` hit a 409 FLOW_TREE_CONFLICT. The gate was green by luck. `run_suites.sh` now waits for Deploy Router runs. Open: echopoint should queue or retry on the tree lock, or the folders flow should use a throwaway org.

whys.problem: A routine suite run failed with 409, and the echopoint deploy gate ran with a real chance of a false red that would hold prod.

because.text: `flow folders` got 409 FLOW_TREE_CONFLICT deleting a folder while the gate's suite ran in the same org.
The flow-tree lock rejects a second writer at once instead of waiting.
The tree lock was designed for one writer per org; concurrent automated writers in one org were not a design case.
The routine started a tag run while a Deploy Router run was in progress.
The soak ran by hand with `flows run --tag`, not through `run_suites.sh`.
The 'never during a gate' rule lived only in SKILL.md; no script checked for an active Deploy Router run.
because.evidence: run_suites.sh before this run had no gate check

because.text: The overlap could have turned the gate red, not only the routine run.
The gate and the dogfood suites share the prod CI org and its `echopointOrgId`, so either side can lose the lock.
Flows that write the folder tree run in the shared CI org instead of a per-run throwaway org.

actions.what: run_suites.sh waits for queued or in-progress Deploy Router runs before each tag (`gate_wait`)
run_suites.sh prints `GATE-OVERLAP` when a Deploy Router run started during a tag
Run every soak through run_suites.sh (or after gate_wait), never a bare `flows run --tag`; noted in SKILL.md
Tree lock: wait briefly or retry on contention instead of failing at once (TryAdvisoryXactLock → bounded wait)
Move `echopoint: flow folders` to a per-run throwaway org so its tree writes never share a lock with the gate

well: The failing execution's timestamps matched the gate's job window within minutes, so the cause was clear without guessing.
wrong: A documented rule with no check in the script was skipped by a hand-run soak.
lucky: The gate's own `flow folders` won the lock; the other order would have held echopoint#779 off prod with a false red.
